text:
R321 — no-MTP prefill retirement and decode expert-cache growth
Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo)
Scope: read-only source/lifetime audit for the owner-specified actual one-shot route in W e3c904e2: 8,192 prefill chunk, 144 expert-cache slots (281 MiB), segmented verifier, no MTP, no prefill borrowing, CPU prefill share/gate off, prefill-first off, compact MoE scratch requested, max context 262,144, int8 KV with 32,768 resident and no KVGrow. No code changes, imports, tests/builds, process/device/model/profiler/GPU work, Git mutation, cleanup, or active Main records inspected. Registry v176 and previous reports R268/275/279/284 were considered to avoid repeating their general lifecycle/capacity conclusions.

Finding
The no-borrow, no-MTP one-shot route has a real opportunity to retire its owned Prefill workspace before decode and use some released physical VRAM for additional expert-cache slots. The best seam is after successful prefill completion, stats collection, and any cache refill/residency upload, but before the verifier is initialized and before decode begins. `Prefill::reset()` drains its compute and copy queues, joins the stager, frees its owned device allocations, then leaves an empty implementation. It does not touch SessionState, its QSA/KV/GDN/PLE state, the KVG arena, or immutable host expert weights. On the specified no-borrow route there are no lent cache slots to restore.

This is materially different from a worker/task tweak: cache size can change which routed experts stay GPU-resident for later decode windows. It could improve hits, but no hit-fraction or speed gain is predicted here because no profile trace for this exact run was inspected and the cache does not evict. The first safe performance comparison should be a modest capacity contrast, not an assumed full 1.8-GiB transfer.

How much Prefill memory is eligible
The 8,192-token Prefill uses individually owned device buffers when `borrow == nullptr`; `Alloc::take` records each allocation in `Prefill::Impl::owned` (src/prefill/prefill.cpp:196–218, 756–770, 783–878). The set includes chunk-sized residual/attention/MoE planes, the max(GDN,QSA,MoE) shared scratch region, expert staging ring, PLE plane, GEMM scratch, fixed tables, and the int8 streamed-KV staging pool when the session is in KV-streaming mode. `release()` frees the owned device pointers after queue drains (538–560). `Prefill::bytes_needed` is a preflight count rather than a physical-free measurement (1064–1106), and it omits separately owned KV staging when `STRATA_KV_STAGE_OWN` is set (497–525).

A retained 8K no-borrow accounting report (R279) records 1,861,857,536 B = 1,775.606 MiB of Prefill `Alloc::take` requests for its exact earlier configuration. That is a useful scale estimate, not a byte promise for this W route: the present W source changed the shared-region rule to `max(gdn_set_bytes,qsa_set_bytes,moe_set_bytes)` (797–800) and gates compact MoE on a pure FP16 fallback with no MMQ (628–639); the exact loaded layout, environment and separately owned staging mode must match before reusing the old count. Current source arithmetic gives a GDN term of about 1,222 MiB at T=8,192 before per-take rounding (571–575); the full prefill workspace is larger because it includes other planes, GEMM scratch, ring, PLE, tables and possibly staged KV. Thus the concrete recoverable amount is the set of actual Prefill-owned GPU allocations at runtime; 1,775.6 MiB is the nearest retained scale, not a measured available-VRAM delta. Reset can also free host-USM/event/stream/stager resources, which should not be added to VRAM.

Cache growth mechanism and simplest seam
Current `ExpertCache::grow(want_bytes)` is not a general expansion API. It works only for `--vram-elastic` segmented caches, and only maps segments inside the address reservation created by `open_segmented` (src/core/expert_cache.cpp:176–217, 267–285; header:116–137). The reservation size is exactly the requested cache payload, with all its segments mapped initially; a 144-slot open does not reserve headroom for more slots. A regular cache is one allocation, so `grow()` rejects it. Simply resetting Prefill therefore does not enlarge the cache.

The cleanest implementation seam for the selected route is to let `ExpertCache` reserve a larger virtual slot range at startup but map only the 144 currently affordable slots, then after Prefill reset map a small tail and populate it from the existing immutable host expert source. This preserves the cache base and existing slot addresses, avoids a VRAM-to-RAM eviction/copy, and puts the new mapping strictly after the large Prefill allocation has been released. Add separate reserved-capacity vs currently-mapped-slot bookkeeping; today `open_segmented` reserves and maps the same `want`, and `slots_` is the full capacity while `live_slots_` is the mapped prefix. Keep profile/residency ownership correct: populate newly mapped slots from the next ranked, nonresident profile entries (or the declared compulsory-fill policy), update host and device residency maps, and never mark a slot resident before its copy completion.

An even more bounded prototype can use a separately opened replacement cache at this same caller seam, but the current public API has no transactional replace operation. Close/reopen changes the device base and all slot offsets, loses cache contents/residency, and must fail closed if the larger open or fill fails. The reserve-larger/map-later approach is safer because it preserves addresses; it also naturally uses `--vram-elastic`'s mapping model. Existing cache open can only preallocate/map its requested slots, so this requires a focused ExpertCache API change before it is runnable.

Reader and state lifetimes
- The one-shot local `Prefill` is declared at generate.cpp:10300; after `prefill.run`, the caller refills any borrowed slots and uploads residency before reporting stats (10384–10424). Under `--no-prefill-borrow`, `lent` stays empty. Copy the Prefill stats before reset because reset clears them (Prefill::reset at 538). No MTP callback/drafter owns Prefill chunk buffers on this route.
- This run's `Verifier` is initialized after the prefill loop at generate.cpp:10675–10683, so its `VerifyHits` copy can consume updated slot offsets/counts once initialized. The route forces/uses segmented verification; confirm the actual host-handoff capability still suppresses the earlier token-graph capture condition at 5541–5544. If a `TokenGraph` was captured, destroy and recapture it after resizing before reuse; never leave graph nodes referring to a retired base or old slot table.
- Before the new verifier initialization, refresh all `Drive`/`TokenHits` cache-base, blob, slot-offset and slot-count fields, plus the stable d_res residency entries. The host expert map is a host vector with device upload; existing cache entries remain resident because the proposed reserve/map path preserves their addresses. The newly mapped slots must be filled from `srcp` before updating `host_res`/d_res.
- Keep SessionState, the full 262,144-cell QSA geometry, int8 KV pool and its current 32,768 resident-cell setting, GDN convolution/recurrent state, PLE state, and any full-context pointers unchanged. `Prefill::reset()` is only workspace retirement; do not reinitialize the session or alter max_context/KV residency to make room. The prompt's final token/decode boundary and output must remain unchanged.
- Preserve the RAM weight source and its ownership through cache fill. Existing immutable source data makes a new GPU slot fill possible without copying evicted experts back from VRAM; read from the loaded source/ranked profile and retain normal source/cache correctness checks.

Bounded comparison after current GEN128 qualification
After the active worker/task matrix closes, compare the current 144-slot cache against a moderate +128-slot mapped tail (272 total slots), keeping the exact same 32K prompt + GEN128 continuation, selected 8K chunk, full 262,144 context, int8 KV resident 32,768, no KVGrow, no MTP, segmented=1, no-borrow, CPU share/gate=0, prefill-first=0, and decode worker/task settings fixed. Use immutable source weights for tail fills. Record actual bytes mapped, exact profile pairs and hashes, new-slot fill time/bytes, host/device residency-map parity, remaining free VRAM before and after mapping, max allocation failure and driver-fault checks. Retain the full-context reservation and reserve policy; stop if post-prefill memory does not admit the tail with safety margin.

Acceptance: the same prompt and continuation IDs/output contract; all old and new slot bytes checked against source; d_res and h_res agree; normal QUIT/health, no async-copy or device faults; clean matched repetitions; separately report prefill and decode wall time, per-window cache hits/misses, and end-to-end decode throughput. Do not infer benefit from an increased cache size alone. If allocation, residency-map, or parity is uncertain, keep the 144-slot configuration.

Prior-evidence corrections and limits
R268 already found the plain `Prefill::reset` workspace-retirement seam and warned that it does not itself enlarge cache. The current task's concrete route is better positioned than the generic R268 discussion because no MTP is active and no cache loan must be refilled; still, full cache replacement is unsafe until pointer owners are rebuilt. R275's MTP/head restoration overlap does not apply to this no-MTP route. R284's 16K alias/GDN tiling capacity projections are unrelated to the selected 8K prefill and are not used here. No exact current-binary allocation count, free-memory delta, route hit fraction, cache-growth success, or latency result is claimed.
